method: Optional compare_heard similarity for previously released intervals up to 8 seconds. No text, image, event name or library of class exemplars enters the audio encoder. Each channel of each original excerpt is analyzed separately at 48 kHz with padding=pad. Cosines describe whole recordings, including ambience. Encoder-only decision below compares the arithmetic mean of all available cross-channel cosines with each candidate. A tie or unavailable side abstains. GPT can choose its own answers. No direct human similarity judgements were collected.

environmental.selection: 50 ESC-50 categories from the existing local archive. Sort within each of the five official supercategories using SHA256(salt reel-auditory-reference-01/). Pair neighbouring categories. For each category select one five-second example and another from a distinct source file and fold. Each of 25 pairs has two target arms. Compare with the original WAVs. For the reader, concatenate A, B and X at their recorded levels and stop at 15 s, one anonymous recording per session. Six pairs selected by hash before any response. Both arms have different target recordings; no target repeats either reference. Labels specify category agreement, not a human listener’s preference.

natural.selection: 24 unmodified locally available Perception Test validation films outside the 44-film audiovisual agreement panel. Distinct films, category-balanced by cycling eligible target labels using the same fixed hash salt before inference. Two non-overlapping earlier sound events and a later X, each between 0.3 and 8 s, mutually separated by 0.1 s with no concurrent event of another class within each excerpt. Exclude generic/muted labels. A or B shares its published sound category with X. The order of A/B is hashed; X is always last. These are naturally occurring events within one staged film and may share production conditions or room noise. No claim of instance, speaker or source identity.
natural.controls_method: Compare absolute clip length difference alone or original pooled RMS difference alone. Noise control replaces each waveform by the same stationary Gaussian noise prefix per film, with its original duration and RMS on each channel. Scores use the real audio encoder.

reader_protocols.specified_comparisons: First 12 selected films and six ESC pairs (12 target trials). Identical instructions across versions. Watch to cutoff in consecutive view turns of up to 8 s with sound_estimates=false and native_audio=false. Call compare_heard twice for the two given reference ranges and the same target. Both spectra, timing, pitch, and recorded levels supplied each time. Disable wording-based descriptions. Request waveform similarity when offered. Hidden reference category labels, fresh session for every arm. Unclear counts as a miss.
reader_protocols.reader_choice: Remaining 12 distinct films. Identical instructions and five tools in both versions. Watch through cutoff with native_audio=false and regular sound estimates. Given only A/B/X times and task, free to use any replay tool or none. No mention of compare_heard, sound similarity, model or scores. New sessions on the deployed code. Fixed films and labels before any free-choice responses. Different films and first-pass sound settings from the specified-comparison group.

absent_target_control.method: Four additional ESC reference pairs outside the six primary reader pairs. Two independent targets per pair: another recording of the same class as A or B, and a recording of a third class in the same ESC supercategory. Exactly the same prompt on matched and unmatched arms, no priors, classes or labels. As in the specified-comparison group, request both comparisons. Answer A, B, neither or unclear. New sessions on both versions; wrong and unclear score zero.

protocol_retry_note: One baseline ESC session completed both media comparisons but timed out before returning an answer. Repeated with the same prompt, inputs and previous version. No retry for a wrong answer or an abstention.
reader_inputs: Filenames, categories and human annotations were hidden from GPT. The archived recording identifiers and event times here locate the originals. A/B orders and target IDs were fixed before the respective sessions.

key_recording.answer: A simple illustration shows a closed brown door against a plain wall, with no visible movement. The audio measurements show a louder, high-frequency change around 4.6–6.5 seconds; its source is uncertain, and the speech check found no intelligible words.

room_only.answer: A closed brown door remains still against a plain wall throughout the clip. The recording appears to contain a very faint, steady hiss-like sound, though its source is uncertain; the two compared intervals are highly similar, and no intelligible words were detected.
